We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to propose route using templates. We have target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. This is a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with para-methyl, the other attached to a cinnamamide (trans double bond) with an anilide bearing an aniline (NH2) on the amide nitrogen? Actually structure: phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Wait: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N: that's trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2 (an aniline attached to amide nitrogen). So overall three fragments: (1) p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? (2) p-phenyl with double bond and amide? Could break at sulfonamide bond (S-N). Also break at amide bond (C=O-N). Also break at C=C? But we need up to 3 steps.

Potential route: Step1: Disconnection of sulfonamide: use sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the other phenyl with side chain). So precursor A: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3). Precursor B: 4-(cinnamoylamino)aniline? Actually the other aromatic with amide and aniline: the phenyl attached to sulfonamide also has the side chain: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. So after sulfonamide formation, we have that phenyl bearing the side chain and sulfonamide N attached to sulfonyl group. So we need that phenyl with side chain and an NH2 (the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl). Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So the amide is -C(=O)-NH-Ph-NH2 (an aniline). So we can disconnect amide: use aniline (aniline) + cinnamoyl chloride (CH=CH-COCl). Then amide formation gives cinnamoyl anilide (C=O-NH-Ph-NH2). Then sulfonylation attaches sulfonyl chloride to the aniline nitrogen? Wait sulfonamide attaches to the aniline nitrogen of the phenyl-sulfonyl side? The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl-sulfonyl group and to the phenyl ring (the one bearing side chain). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the phenyl-sulfonyl group attached to the phenyl ring (the one with side chain). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl-sulfonyl group and to the phenyl ring (the side chain phenyl). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is not the same as the amide nitrogen. So the phenyl ring bearing side chain also has a sulfonamide N attached to sulfonyl group. So that phenyl ring has an NH attached to sulfonyl group (SO2) and also attached to side chain (C=C-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of that phenyl ring (attached to the ring). So we need a precursor: the phenyl ring with side chain and an NH (as an aniline) that can be sulfonylated. That precursor is 4-(cinnamoylamino)aniline? Actually the phenyl ring is substituted at para position with sulfonamide N (attached to sulfonyl group) and at para? Wait original SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So first phenyl (tolyl) has NSO2 attached to second phenyl. The second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) is attached to sulfonyl group via S(=O)(=O)-N- (the N attached to first phenyl). Actually NS(=O)(=O)c2... means the N of first phenyl is attached to sulfonyl group, which is attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is on the tolyl ring (aniline). So tolyl ring has NH-SO2-Ph. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of tolyl ring. So we can disconnect at N-S bond: tolyl aniline (p-toluidine) + sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So step1: sulfonylation of p-toluidine with sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl with side chain.

Thus we need sulfonyl chloride precursor: 4-(cinnamoylamino)phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring (the second phenyl) which also has side chain at para? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl group attaches to that phenyl at position 1 (maybe para to side chain). So we need 4-(cinnamoylamino)phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-para-(C=C-CO-NH-Ph-NH2)). So step2: synthesis of that sulfonyl chloride from corresponding sulfonic acid or from sulfonylation of that phenyl with chlorosulfonic acid? Could be from 4-(cinnamoylamino)benzenesulfonic acid then convert to chloride. Or we could start from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride) and then amide formation? But the amide is on the phenyl ring, not on the sulfonyl group. So we could start from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and then acylate the amine with cinnamoyl chloride to give sulfonyl chloride still present? Wait the amine is on the phenyl ring, we need to attach the side chain to that phenyl via amide. So we could start from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride). Then perform amide formation with cinnamoyl chloride to give 4-(cinnamoylamido)benzenesulfonyl chloride. That is step2 (amide formation). Then step1 sulfonylation with p-toluidine gives final product.

Thus total steps: 2 steps (amide formation, then sulfonylation). Leaves: p-toluidine (commercial), cinnamoyl chloride (commercial), p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). All likely cheap.

We need to verify templates for amide formation (acyl chloride + amine) and sulfonylation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Use search to find templates.

Search for amide formation: functional_groups_formed amide, reactants include acyl chloride and amine. Let's search with criteria: functional_groups_formed ["amide"], functional_groups_broken maybe ["amine"]? But we can just search for amide formation templates.
